segments.t: As Denis and Katya step into the apartment kitchen, Denis's roommate Senya and his wife Marina greet them. Senya immediately jokes about Denis's overnight guest until Marina invites the young couple to eat breakfast together. Let's listen to their cheerful breakfast conversation in Russian.
Now let's go through the breakfast conversation in the kitchen line by line.
'Hey there, who do we have here?' Senya opens with a casual colloquial greeting and an interrogative pronoun in a possessive construction.
'Hello, I was giving her tea.' Denis replies politely and uses a masculine past verb with the instrumental singular of tea.
'Good morning to all of you.' Katya offers the standard neuter morning greeting followed by a plural dative pronoun phrase.
'Senya, why are you embarrassing people?' A colloquial question word meaning why here accompanies a transitive verb and an animate accusative plural object.
'All right, let's go have breakfast together.' An inclusive plural imperative of motion takes an imperfective infinitive meaning to eat breakfast.
'Have you two been dating for a long time?' Russian uses the present tense with an adverb meaning long ago for an action that continues now.
'Well, there is a very long story there.' A conversational particle and spatial adverb introduce a feminine nominative noun phrase.
'We have been friends for a very long time.' The first-person plural present verb expresses an ongoing friendship that started in the past.
'And we are only dating starting today.' A reciprocal reflexive verb in the first-person plural contrasts their long friendship with their new romance.
'Today will be our first day.' The future form of to be links the temporal adverb to an ordinal numeral and masculine noun.
'Yes, Katyusha, eat up, eat.' Denis uses an affectionate diminutive form of Katya's name and repeats a singular imperative of eating.
'Thank you, everything is very tasty.' Katya praises the meal with a polite word of thanks and a short neuter predicate adverb. Let's listen to the full kitchen dialogue again without interruption.

Denis proudly explains that he and Katya have been friends for a long time and are starting their first day as a couple. Listen for the reciprocal reflexive verbs meaning to be friends and to date. See you in the next scene.
